name: TX-33
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+18 partisan lean makes the seat structurally Democratic
Colin Allred brings strong name recognition and $7.4 million raised versus a Republican opponent with no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 98%
No public general-election polling, so the open-seat margin carries some uncertainty
model.rationale: An D+18 Dallas-area seat, a well-funded and well-known Democratic nominee in Colin Allred against a Republican with no visible financial operation, and market pricing near 98% all align on a comfortable Democratic hold despite the open seat.
model.watch: A sharp drop in Democratic turnout in the low-profile open-seat race, or late negative news about Allred, would be the main threats to the expected margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jasmine Crockett (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Texas's 33rd District, anchored in Dallas, carries a Democratic partisan lean of roughly 18 points, and the open seat created by Jasmine Crockett's Senate bid remains firmly in the party's column. Democrats nominated Colin Allred, a former congressman and 2024 Senate nominee with strong name recognition, who has raised about $7.4 million. Republican Patrick Gillespie reports no fundraising figures and has attracted little outside spending on either side.

No public general-election polls are available, so the picture rests on district fundamentals. Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 98%, and the current national environment adds to the party's edge. The main unknowns are typical of open seats: turnout patterns and name recognition outside the district's core. The underlying partisanship makes a Democratic hold the clear expectation, with the remaining question being the size of the winning margin.
